name: The Carroll Oak

location.address: Birr Castle Demesne, Rosse Row, Birr, Co. Offaly R42 VO27

official_register.name: Heritage Trees of Ireland (Tree Council of Ireland / Aubrey Fennell), record 508, 'Named trees'

access: Paid entry to Birr Castle Demesne (120 acres, about 10 km of walks); admission price and opening times are on birrcastle.retailint-tickets.com, open all year with seasonal hours (UCC Tree Explorers). Dogs on leads. The castle itself is a private home.
transport: Birr town centre, demesne gate on Rosse Row; no rail in Birr, nearest stations Tullamore and Portlaoise need a bus or taxi (Local Link, Kearns Bus). Pay-and-display parking opposite the entrance.
verify_notes: Owner of the ground (birrcastle.com/wildlife) says the demesne's oldest tree is the Carroll Oak, 'certainly planted before the Parsons family arrived in 1620' (the O'Carroll clan held the castle until the 1620s; the page does not say which family planted it). Irish Times 28 May 2005 ('In Birr's botanic wonderland'): the O'Carroll oak 'planted about 455 years ago' (so about 1550), 'set to last roughly as long again', with a carefully trimmed circle around the base. Register record 508 (13 Aug 2009): Quercus robur, 'Named trees', maiden form, band 300-500 years, evidence of significant habitat. Ages differ: 455 years in 2005 means about 480 now; one guide says over 500 (not fetched). Age here is a broad band from those, not a measurement. No girth or height found. Alive: lifecheck RECENT, an iNaturalist observation 2025-03-30 within range of the register point (not confirmed to be this trunk), and the owner's current page still names it. PIN: register grid N054052 = 53.09792,-7.91842, 100 m precision, ~330 m NW of the castle coordinate (53.09536,-7.91476) which may mean the converted points sit skewed; treat as parkland-level. Birr's Tree Trail (5 km, 65 trees) is on the estate site but its list is not published. RECOGNITION CANDIDATE: a single broad old oak in open parkland with a neatly trimmed circle kept clear around its base.

name: The Birr Castle Box Hedges

location.address: Formal Gardens, lower terrace, Birr Castle Demesne, Rosse Row, Birr, Co. Offaly R42 VO27

official_register.name: Heritage Trees of Ireland, record 79 ('Arboricultural curiosities', avenue of multi-stem box)

access: Paid entry to Birr Castle Demesne; the Formal Gardens are inside the ticketed grounds. Admission price and hours are on birrcastle.retailint-tickets.com. Castle interior not included.
transport: Birr town centre, demesne gate on Rosse Row; nearest stations Tullamore and Portlaoise need a bus or taxi (Local Link, Kearns Bus).
verify_notes: FLAGGED: ensemble, not one tree, and the height and age sources disagree. Owner (birrcastle.com) states 'the worlds tallest box hedging' on the lower terrace of the Formal Gardens (no height). Wikipedia: box hedges over 300 years old, tallest hedge in the world per Guinness. Search results (not fetched pages, so pointers only): Atlas Obscura about 40 ft (about 12 m), Lonely Planet planted 1780s and 12 m, Irish Times 31 ft, Fodor's 32 ft. Height here (12 m) is the most cited but the owner gives none; the upper bound of 12 m is unverified, the safe range is 9 to 12 m. Planting date: 1780s versus over 300 years (see age range). Register record 79 (13 Aug 2009): Buxus sempervirens, avenue, multi-stem, band 200-300 years, at grid N056054 = 53.10008,-7.91619, which is ~500 m north of the castle and does not fit 'lower terrace of the Formal Gardens' beside the castle; so either the converted point is skewed or the record is a different box avenue. The pin here is the castle coordinate as a stand-in for the Formal Gardens, deliberately parkland-level approximate. One place to stand (the hedge walk on the lower terrace) so it fits a collectible ensemble; the writer may decide whether a hedge is wanted. RECOGNITION CANDIDATE: a pair of enormous, clipped box walls forming a green corridor on the lower terrace of the formal gardens, rising above head height several times over.

name: Birr Dawn Redwood

location.address: Birr Castle Demesne, Rosse Row, Birr, Co. Offaly R42 VO27

official_register.name: Heritage Trees of Ireland, record 355 ('Exceptional specimen trees')

access: Paid entry to Birr Castle Demesne; open all year with seasonal hours. Price and hours on birrcastle.retailint-tickets.com.
transport: Birr town centre, demesne gate on Rosse Row; nearest stations Tullamore and Portlaoise need a bus or taxi (Local Link, Kearns Bus).
verify_notes: FLAGGED: owner's page does not locate or measure the tree; link between owner's sentence and register record is by species and age band only. Owner (birrcastle.com/?p=5219): the first Metasequoia discovered reached Birr as seed in the 1940s, and 'a fine tree from that period' still stands. Register record 355 (13 Aug 2009): Metasequoia glyptostroboides, maiden, 'Exceptional specimen trees', band 50-100 years, grid N052054 = 53.0995,-7.92109 (100 m precision). A 1940s seed would give about 80 years. Lifecheck NONE. No girth or height. A dawn redwood was only described to science in 1941-1948, so seed this early is plausible; the 'first discovered' wording is the owner's, kept as theirs. Worth the walk rather less than the oak: it is a notable specimen of a famous living fossil rather than a veteran. RECOGNITION CANDIDATE: a tall, feathery, fluted-trunk conifer that turns bronze in autumn and drops its needles in winter.
